Ardsley & Robin Hood — Leeds, United Kingdom

Relatively safer day Relatively safer night

In detail

West Yorkshire Police recorded 420 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — an average of 6.0 per 1,000 residents a month, the 29th highest rate of Leeds's 33 wards. The daytime score here is driven by burglary (6), shoplifting (5), vehicle crime (5); the evening/night score by violent crime (63), anti social behaviour (14), public order (14). Those two scores are split by offence type, not by clock time — the police feed records no time of day, so day and night here mean the kinds of crime typical of each, not counts of incidents observed then. Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

Frequently asked questions

Is Ardsley & Robin Hood safe?

Wandroz currently rates Ardsley & Robin Hood in Leeds as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Leeds, both by day and after dark. This rating is derived from West Yorkshire Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is Ardsley & Robin Hood safe at night?

At night, Ardsley & Robin Hood is rated as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Leeds. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Ardsley & Robin Hood a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Ardsley & Robin Hood's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Leeds) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
